title: Waiver of a Benefit Overpayment — Notice of the Claimant's Rights
content:
A waiver forgives the unpaid principal of a Benefit Overpayment Accounts debt that arose without fault on the claimant's part when recovering it would defeat the purpose of benefits.

## Who may be granted a waiver

Only an overpayment whose classification is waiver-eligible may be waived; claimant-error and fraud overpayments are never waived. The classification is the one shown on the Department's overpayment record, and it governs both the opening of a review and any waiver adjustment.

## The request is the claimant's own application

The waiver request is the claimant's own application, giving household size and annual household income, and the agent opens the review only from a request the claimant has lodged. The request must be on the Department's waiver request records and tied to the overpayment concerned.

## The time limit

A waiver request is accepted only when it is received no later than the waiver request window after the overpayment determination date. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the overpayment determination date, and a request received on the last day is timely. The determination date is the one on the overpayment record; the date received is the one on the waiver request record. The waiver-eligible classifications carry a window of 30 days; the others carry 0, waiver not being available to them.

| Determination date (hypothetical) | Day 1 of the window | Last day (day 30) | Request received | Accepted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 March | 3 March | 1 April | 1 April | Yes, received on the last day |
| 2 March | 3 March | 1 April | 2 April | No, received after the last day |
| 2 March | 3 March | 1 April | 2 March | Yes, received before the window ends |

## While the request is under review

A timely request taken under review moves the overpayment to waiver pending, whether recovery had begun or not. While the review is open, offsets, intercepts and billing stop, but voluntary repayments are still accepted. When an appeal of the same determination is pending, the appeal is decided first and the waiver review waits.

## The decision — clause no longer in force

The clause reading "The decision follows the household income percent of the poverty guideline: at or below the full-waiver percent the whole unpaid principal is waived; above it and at or below the partial-waiver percent the partial share of the unpaid principal is waived, rounded to the cent, and the rest stays in recovery; above the partial-waiver percent the waiver is denied." is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the Department's current basis for deciding waiver requests.

## What a waiver covers

A waiver covers only the principal unpaid on the decision date; amounts already recovered are not refunded.
